sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Financial Market News Aggregation and Syndication Feed

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU (Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union) Bilateral Investment Treaty with [various countries]
Luxembourg-United States Double Taxation Treaty (signed 1996, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (Loi du 12 novembre 2004 relative au blanchiment et au financement du terrorisme), as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Loi du 13 janvier 2019 instituant un Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs), as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 implementing the RBE; Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/2155 and relevant CSSF regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Partnership Agreement (Contrat de société) of the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the jurisdiction of origin (if notarised) or legal counsel (if private writing)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Non-Due or Certificate of Name Clearance (Certificat de non-confusion)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCSL)
Corporate domiciliation / registered agent in Luxembourg

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration and supporting identification documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, legal representatives, directors and partners against the consolidated EU financial sanctions list, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, and the Luxembourg national sanctions list (Liste nationale des sanctions) administered by the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance. Additional PEP checks are required for all clients determined to be high risk or acting in a syndicated finance context, in accordance with CSSF Circular 15/01 and the Law of 12 November 2004. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is mandatory for any politically exposed person, including by establishing the source of wealth and funds. The screening must be performed prior to incorporation, at UBO designation, and on an ongoing basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) – electronic portal available via guichet.lu and RCSL eDesk. The name clearance process is coordinated through the Ministry of Justice and the RCSL.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be written in Latin characters and may be in any language, provided a Luxembourgish-, French-, or German-language transliteration is available for official filings. The name must necessarily contain the legal form designation 'Société en commandite spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp' for partnerships opting to abbreviate. Non-Latin scripts require an official transliteration in French or German for registration in the RCSL.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank or Banque (requires approval of the Ministry of Finance and may trigger banking licensing)
Assurance / Insurance (requires approval of the Financial Sector Supervisory Commission – CSSF)
État / State / Government / Luxembourg (requires ministerial approval to avoid misleading connotations)
Fiduciaire / Trust (requires express approval from the Ministry of Justice)
S.A. / S.à r.l. / SCA (cannot be used for an SCSp, as these correspond to distinct corporate forms)
Terrorist, Sanctioned, or any terms implying an illegal purpose (entirely prohibited)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed name due to confusion, public policy, or the use of an insufficiently distinctive token, the applicant may file a formal administrative appeal to the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice within one month from the receipt of the rejection notice. Simultaneously, an application can be made to the President of the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) acting in commercial matters for a declaratory order that the name does not conflict with third-party rights. The appeal must be in French or German, accompanied by the original name clearance request, the rejection letter, and any evidence of prior first-to-file title. The decision of the District Court may be further appealed to the Court of Appeal (Cour d'appel) within 40 days. Extension of a name reservation is not generally permitted; however, a new application for the same name may be filed after the initial 60-day window lapses, provided no intervening conflicting name has been registered.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally permissible in Luxembourg for an SCSp conducting a low-risk financial newswire API business, provided that a physical registered office is nonetheless established in Luxembourg by way of a corporate domiciliation service. The virtual office must involve a reliable and fully managed correspondence address, a physical presence comprising employer or management oversight in case of regulatory inquiries, and compliance with the registered office obligations under the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended. The virtual office must be provided by a registered corporate domiciliation agent in accordance with the Law of 31 May 1999 governing the occupancy of a registered office (Loi du 31 mai 1999). A simple post-office box or purely electronic virtual office will not meet the statutory substance requirements. The SCSp must maintain its central administration place in Luxembourg, and the newswire API activity must achieve taxable nexus in Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: for a low-risk financial newswire aggregation and syndicated finance feed activity, the probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Luxembourg Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA), the Trade and Companies Register, or the Centralised Criminal Justice Body (Parquet) is estimated at 8-12% within the first three years of operation. The risk increases if the company claims special substance benefits or if a shareholder is a high-risk PEP. Annual compliance reviews by the corporate domiciliation agent will be performed.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance application / Certificat de non-confusion to the RCSL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RCSL fee schedule, generally €35 for a name certificate (converted to USD at prevailing exchange rate)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarisation of the SCSp partnership agreement (if notarised)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff scale based on the partnership agreement value and complexity; statutory disbursements included

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille for foreign-origin documents (partnership agreement, UBO passport copies, address evidence)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs / Upstream competent authority in document country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: €15 per document under the 1961 Apostille Convention, converted and aggregated for six documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Original notarial deed registration with the RCSL and entry into the Trade and Companies Register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCSL back-office registration fee for limited partnerships; €220 standard plus electronic filing surcharge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation excerpt in the official gazette 'Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations' (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Publication Office of the Luxembourg Government (Central Legislation Service)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official publication statutory rate per extract, approximately €110

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration filing with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: There is no filing fee for the first UBO declaration; a third-party professional processing fee is charged

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office (domiciliation) service annual fee – first year pro-rata
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg corporate domiciliation agent (regulated alternative investment fund / corporate service provider)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a low-risk service company under RBE and criminal law compliance requirements, approximately €2,000/yr

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal and tax structuring advisory for SCSp formation and syndicated finance newswire API (pre-incorporation readiness)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for an SCSp formation with a moderate-height AML/KYC package, excluding ongoing compliance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial PEP and sanctions screening run (OPAC, UN, EU, Luxembourg national list) for all UBOs and authorised partners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Regulated screening technology provider / outsourced compliance vendor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Subscription-based KYC/AML screening software, per-person rate and jurisdiction surcharge

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 1, 27-30 and Articles 902-1 et seq. (SCSp regime inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013 on Alternative Investment Funds)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers office; RBE unit for beneficial ownership; RESA electronic gazette for legal publication
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Constitutive partnership agreement (contrat de société / société en commandite spéciale) executed by private deed or notarial deed, together with the RCS declaration form (Formulaire B) and the appointment of the manager (gérant), filed electronically via LBRonline
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The SCSp has no statutory minimum subscribed or paid-up capital; contributions are freely determined in the partnership agreement and no bank blocked-account or escrow certificate is required for registration, unless contractually agreed between the partners
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: 1. RESOLVED, that the constitutive partnership agreement (contrat de société) of the SCSp is hereby approved in final form, with each founder's capital contribution credited as stated in the financial contribution schedule. 2. RESOLVED, that the registered office shall be located at [Registered Office Address], L- Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. 3. RESOLVED, that [Manager Name] is appointed as sole manager (gérant) of the SCSp with full management power. 4. RESOLVED, that the manager is authorized to open bank accounts, execute all RCS and beneficial-ownership filings, and publish the required notice in the RESA. 5. RESOLVED, that this Resolution is effective upon issuance of the RCS certificate of registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding partners (internal act); optional notarization before a Luxembourg notary if real estate is contributed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp partnership agreement with the commercial name, duration, object, registered office address, contribution schedule, allocation of profits and losses, and management powers. The agreement must be signed by all general partners and limited partners. If executed by private deed, each partner must sign in person or by power of attorney; no notarial deed is mandatory unless an immovable asset is contributed. The signature pages and capital contribution schedule are annexed.
required_dossiers: Partnership agreement (contrat de société) in French, German, or English version
Certified copy of passport or national ID of each founding partner
Proof of residential or registered address of each partner
Financial contribution schedule or proof of contribution in kind report
Power of attorney if any partner signs by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed is refused by the RCS or a bank due to irregular wording or missing annexes, the partners may execute a rectifying addendum (avenant) and refile; defective signatures are cured by fresh execution or by legalization before a Luxembourg notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit RCS incorporation filing via LBRonline
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed partnership agreement and Form B electronically through the LBRonline portal. The application must include the appointed manager's details, registered office confirmation, and the statutory declaration that the formation requirements are met. Pay the prescribed filing fee via the online gateway. The RCS will issue a certificate of registration and assign a Luxembourg registration number (RCS number).
required_dossiers: Signed partnership agreement
Form B (notice of appointment of manager and registered office)
Declaration of acceptance by the manager (gérant)
Residential certificate or lease agreement for the registered office
Evidence of payment of filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (à compléter), the applicant must cure the deficiency within the notified deadline by submitting corrected documents, a certified French or German translation, or the legalized signature page. A refusal may be challenged before the Luxembourg district court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within forty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish in RESA and obtain the national identification number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: LBR publication service (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations - RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the RCS automatically triggers publication of the statutory excerpt in the RESA. The excerpt includes the SCSp name, registered office, object, managers, and capital information. Concurrently, the RCS allocates a national business number (numéro d'identification) which is used for tax and social security correspondence.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
RCS excerpt data already filed in step 2
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication contains errors, the manager files a rectification request with the RCS; corrections are published at minimal cost. Failure to publish is cured by prompt supplementary filing, and late fees may apply after notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register beneficial owners with the RBE
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, submit the RBE declaration identifying each ultimate beneficial owner (natural persons) holding more than 25% interest, control through other means, or senior management if no direct owner is identified. File online via LBRonline; access to the public is restricted to legitimate interest under the current legal framework.
required_dossiers: RBE declaration form for the SCSp
Identification documents of each ultimate beneficial owner
Ownership or control structure schematic
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE rejects the declaration due to incomplete ownership details, the manager must provide a supplementary ownership statement and correct the filing. Administrative fines apply for non-compliance; remedies include submitting a revised declaration within fifteen days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete VAT and direct tax registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and Administration des contributions directes (ACD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp for Luxembourg VAT if the newswire services are provided in the course of economic activity; apply for a VAT number and, where applicable, the intra-Community identification number. Because the SCSp is tax-transparent for corporate income tax purposes, file Form 5 (non-resident declarative return) if required, and obtain Luxembourg provisional tax account references for the partners.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration
VAT registration form (Formulaire 1A)
Copy of partnership agreement and RBE confirmation
Description of services provided and target clients
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT does not assign a VAT number, the taxpayer can request a formal reminder and remedy by submitting the missing revenue estimates. Objections to tax registration are filed within three months of the notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain business establishment permit and occupational clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy, Direction générale des classes moyennes; Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) if the SCSp acts as a merchant or the manager performs a regulated commercial activity; the application includes proof of good repute, professional qualifications, and a sworn statement. For the physical office, obtain the fire safety certificate from the communal authority or CGDIS and ensure compliance with ITM workplace rules; register as an employer with the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) when staff are hired.
required_dossiers: Business permit application form for commercial activity
Criminal record extract (bulletin n° 3) of the manager
Office lease contract and floor plan
Fire safety inspection certificate (CGDIS or commune)
Employer registration form with the CCSS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of the Economy rejects the permit, the applicant may appeal to the administrative tribunal within three months and submit additional evidence of professional competence; fire safety deficiencies are cured by implementing remediation measures and re-inspection within the prescribed schedule.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Direction générale des classes moyennes) for general business establishment; no sectoral regulator for pure financial newswire aggregation; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) is not applicable absent regulated financial services
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) - required only if the SCSp or its manager exercises a merchant or regulated activity in Luxembourg; otherwise not required for a passive partnership

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - category non-listed office-based information service with no industrial installation, no IPPC/IED activity, and no physical production process
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A - office operations only; comply with communal wastewater ordinance, waste segregation rules, and WEEE directive for electronic equipment; no VOC or industrial emission thresholds apply

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) from the competent commune or CGDIS for the registered office; structural load inspection of office floors if IT server racks are installed; occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering workstations, electrical safety, and ergonomic premises

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority (Administration des contributions directes, ACD) - portal acd.public.lu; Luxembourg Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA, AEDT) - VAT portal pvat.public.lu; unified e-government filing portal MyGuichet.lu; commercial registry operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate the SCSp (Societe en Commandite Speciale) by notarial or private deed and register the filing with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu); obtain the RCS matricule (national business identification number) and proof of registered office in Luxembourg. Step 2 - For indirect taxes, submit the AEDT VAT registration application through the MyGuichet.lu single portal; the AEDT assigns the SCSp a Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU + 8 digits. Because the SCSp is statutorily fiscally transparent, it does not obtain a separate corporate income-tax TIN; it files an annual partnership information return, and each partner - including foreign investors and the corporate or individual general partner - is taxed on its allocable share. Non-resident partners must obtain a Luxembourg direct-tax matricule and file a non-resident tax return where the SCSp's commercial activity in Luxembourg creates a permanent establishment for them under the applicable double tax treaty. Foreign entities acting as investors or as corporate general partner must supply certified corporate existence and tax residence certificates at registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - the SCSp is statutorily fiscally transparent under Luxembourg law (Article 50 of the Law of 12 July 2013 on alternative investment funds and Circular L.I.R. No. 14/3). It is not subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax or net wealth tax; income, gains, deductions and credits flow through to partners. For VAT, the AEDT applies fiscal transparency to contractual partnerships without legal personality where the SCSp lacks independent economic activity, but the SCSp remains a liable person for VAT administration and must satisfy registration, invoicing and return obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no check-the-box regime; legal form governs tax classification. Available statutory elections: (i) VAT grouping election under Article 60 of the VAT Law, allowing the SCSp to join a VAT group with its general partner and affiliates (joint and several VAT liability applies); (ii) real-estate VAT option under Articles 44-45 of the VAT Law, waiving exempt treatment for real estate supplies; (iii) OSS / non-Union OSS election on the EU One-Stop-Shop portal for B2C electronic services, permitting Luxembourg VAT compliance for cross-border supplies to consumers in other Member States; (iv) partnership profit-allocation election, where the partnership agreement can define profit shares, subject to substance and economic-contribution defences; and (v) ATAD 2 hybrid-mismatch alignment, where a foreign jurisdiction characterises the SCSp as opaque, requiring automatic counter-measures for double deduction or non-inclusion rather than a taxpayer election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - taxe sur la valeur ajoutee), governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 as amended and harmonised with EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC; administered by the AEDT, with standard rate 17%, intermediate rate 14%, reduced rate 8% and super-reduced rate 3%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 - annual taxable turnover threshold for the VAT small-business exemption (franchise) under Article 47 of the Luxembourg VAT Law (raised from EUR 15,000 to EUR 35,000 effective 1 July 2020). The franchise is unavailable to non-established foreign suppliers and to persons opting into the normal regime; foreign suppliers making taxable supplies in Luxembourg have no turnover threshold and must register from the first supply, or use OSS for EU B2C e-services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: A phased B2B e-invoicing mandate applies under the Luxembourg e-invoicing law adopted in 2024: from 1 January 2025, every Luxembourg-established taxable person must be able to receive structured electronic invoices; from 1 January 2026, such taxable persons must issue structured e-invoices (e.g. Peppol BIS 3.0, EN 16931/UBL format) to Luxembourg-established B2B customers, unless the recipient is outside scope. Luxembourg does not operate a real-time tax-authority clearance (continuous transaction controls) or digital-stamping system; e-invoices flow over the Peppol network without prior tax-authority validation. E-invoice metadata is accessible to the AEDT during audits. For cross-border B2C e-services (financial newswire API subscriptions), the EU One-Stop-Shop portal (Union OSS and non-Union OSS) is the statutory e-reporting and remittance channel; intra-EU B2B services are reported via quarterly recapitulative statements, not through e-invoice clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports: physical export of goods from the EU customs territory qualifies for zero rating under Article 62 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, provided the supplier obtains proof of exit (accepted customs export declaration and transport documents) and retains it for the statutory record-keeping period. Services: the financial newswire API constitutes electronically supplied services (Annex II, EU VAT Directive); where supplied to a taxable customer outside Luxembourg (intra-EU or third-country), Luxembourg VAT is reverse-charged or is outside territorial scope (B2B place of supply at the customer's establishment); where supplied to an end consumer resident outside the EU, no Luxembourg VAT arises (place of supply is the customer's residence). The SCSp must document the non-Luxembourg or non-EU status of each customer (validated VAT ID via VIES for EU business customers, business registration or residence evidence for third-country customers), the executed subscription or API framework agreement, and the actual receipt of consideration through the selected payment rails (SWIFT wire or Stripe). Input VAT on costs attributable to zero-rated or outside-scope exports remains creditable, and the resulting credit is refundable through the periodic Luxembourg VAT return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / EU customs declaration accepted at the office of export, with MRN reference and exit confirmation at the office of exit)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR consignment note proving physical exit from the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice and export contract evidencing the international consignment chain (supplier, buyer, consignee)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement proving receipt of export proceeds on the SCSp's account
For services: customer's foreign business registration or VAT ID, executed subscription or API framework agreement, and digital usage logs or API authentication records supporting service delivery
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg law imposes no statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; the 180-day parameter is applied here as a documentary-substantiation benchmark and commercial prudential standard. Failure to evidence receipt of export proceeds within a reasonable period may prompt the AEDT to question economic reality and to disallow zero rating. If export zero rating is insufficiently documented, the AEDT retroactively claws back the VAT exemption and assesses Luxembourg VAT at 17% plus late-payment interest (currently 0.6% per month or fraction of a month) and, in cases of negligence, an administrative penalty that can reach up to 100% of the evaded tax. Intentional misstatement or false export documentation constitutes tax fraud (fraude fiscale) under the Luxembourg General Tax Law as strengthened by the Law of 6 March 2019, carrying imprisonment of up to five years and significant criminal fines, as well as loss of good tax standing. Customs-law non-compliance (inaccurate export declarations) triggers penalties under Article 42 of the Union Customs Code as implemented in Luxembourg customs law, together with post-clearance recovery of customs duties within applicable statutory limitation periods (generally up to three years, extended where prosecutable offences are present). The AEDT recovery period for under-assessed VAT is generally up to five years, extended to ten years where fraudulent intent is shown. Refund claims built on sham export paper are treated as unjustified VAT refunds and are clawed back with the above penalties plus interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the prudential and AML/CFT supervision authority for credit institutions and payment services.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is the sole legal tender; Luxembourg applies full capital and current account convertibility under the EU Treaty and the EU Capital Movements Directive (Article 63 TFEU). No exchange controls exist for non-resident investors; profit and dividend remittances are unrestricted. Deductions or distributions are subject only to standard corporate, withholding tax, and DAC6/ATAD reporting obligations. Balance-of-payments statistical reporting to the BCL is mandatory for resident enterprises for cross-border flows above EUR 12,500 per transaction, but this constitutes statistical monitoring, not approval or restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or conversion requirements apply. Luxembourg and the euro area impose no mandated timeline or ratio for converting export or service receipts into local currency. Receipts in foreign currency may be retained, converted, or hedged freely; only statistical balance-of-payments declarations to the BCL are required where applicable.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Luxembourg-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions (PIs), whether domestic or passporting under PSD2, are viable for operational sub-accounts and low-value newswire subscription receipts. Offshore digital EMIs without an EU/EEA licence or Luxembourg passport are legally barred from providing payment services to a Luxembourg entity on a cross-border basis; capital escrow and regulatory funds must be held with a fully licensed credit institution. Fintech EMIs generally cannot issue documentary credits or offer commercial LC capacity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is not statutorily mandated. Under CSSF AML/CFT rules and bank-specific KYC policies, remote onboarding is permitted where robust video identification and e-signature procedures are used, typically accompanied by a sworn statutory declaration from the managing partner or director. In practice, most tier-1 Luxembourg banks require an in-person or video-verified interview with at least one senior director or ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), and legal counsel or a regulated fund administrator may serve as an introducer under CSSF Circular 20/744 guidance on virtual assets only by analogy; standard practice favours a physical or high-grade video interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners or directors domiciled in high-risk or non-EU jurisdictions without prior regulated-banking references.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised passport copies and proof of address; legalised or apostilled certificate of incorporation; clean tax residence certificates; bank reference letter from an EU/EEA regulated institution in the prior six months; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; organisational chart evidencing the full UBO chain up to natural persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unregulated commercial model of financial newswire data aggregation and syndication generating a high-volume, low-value cross-border invoice profile that resembles money remittance patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial agreements with each subscriber and content licensor; pro-forma invoices and payment schedules; list of counterparties validated through KYB checks; historical transaction log from a pre-existing bank or FinTech provider; written business narrative describing the API subscription and syndication flow; data licensing registry records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp pass-through tax classification and absence of statutory legal personality may create ambiguity regarding the account holder and authorised signatories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership agreement (contrat de société); certificate of registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS); certificate evidencing non-legal-personality status and representative capacity; CSSF-registered professional of the financial sector acting as administrator or AML agent; legal opinion from a Luxembourg law firm confirming the SCSp's capacity to hold accounts and execute treasury transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multiple or frequent third-party payments to offshore media or data infrastructure providers with no established trade background.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vendor due-diligence file for each provider; Master Services Agreements and service-level agreements; SWIFT confirmation history; beneficial ownership declarations of counterparties; regulatory licences of counterparties where applicable; declaration of consistency between contractual purpose and payment amount.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: for equity and shareholder loans into the Luxembourg SCSp, use SWIFT MT103 via the injecting bank to the BIC of the SCSp's Luxembourg account; SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA CT) with the dedicated purpose code 'B040' or 'C001' or an accurately aligned ECB BOP statistical code, depending on the commercial substance; purpose code 'EQUI' or 'N005' (equity injection) is commonly accepted by BCL for balance-of-payments reporting. Verification bundle: signed capital call notice, subscribed partnership units or contribution deed, board or managing partner resolution, bank debit/credit advices, and a confirmation from the Luxembourg registered office. No CSSF or BCL prior approval is required for inbound capital transfers, but all amounts must be declared to the BCL via the resident enterprise's statistical reporting channel.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: operational expenses, licensing fees, and subscription settlement to EU counterparties are executed via SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) or SEPA Credit Transfer; for non-EU vendors, use SWIFT MT103 with relevant purpose codes (e.g., '2001' for services or '2010' for financial services fees). Where the newswire syndication business requires guarantee of payment against delivery of data licences, a commercial letter of credit (documentary credit, UCP 600) issued by the Luxembourg account bank in favour of the content provider is permissible; the SCSp conducts treasury transactions exclusively through its regulated Luxembourg bank account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) with EU/EEA authorised credit institutions where settlement is in euro

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year, no later than 31 December; updates must be filed within one month of any transfer or change in beneficial ownership/control.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible officers may face criminal fines up to EUR 1,250,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years for deliberate non-compliance; persistent default may trigger judicial strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing and statutory disclosure to the Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Where the disclosure obligation applies, within 7 months after financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, filing by 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines up to EUR 5,000; coercive court-ordered filing; prolonged non-compliance can lead to administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is triggered by exceeding any two of the following Luxembourg thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4,400,000, net turnover EUR 8,800,000, and average full-time workforce of 50 employees. Regulated AIF/SCSp vehicles are subject to mandatory audit under CSSF rules regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts and EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS is permitted for consolidated accounts and regulated investment fund structures.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp has no separate legal personality, but must still maintain RBE registration. Beneficial ownership details must be confirmed annually by 31 December and updated within one month of any transfer of limited partnership interests or change in general partner control. The register must identify all ultimate beneficial owners, including any partner holding more than 25% of capital or votes or otherwise directing the partnership.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (for an SCSp: register of limited partners and general partner holdings)
Register of Directors (for an SCSp: register of general partner corporate officers and appointed managers)
Minute Book (for an SCSp: minutes of partners' meetings and general partner resolutions)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City composite: 17% corporate income tax + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax; municipal rate varies by commune)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A Luxembourg SCSp is fiscally transparent and is not within the scope of corporate income tax or municipal business tax; taxable income is allocated to partners. For corporate partners that are tax resident or carrying on a Luxembourg permanent establishment, preferential regimes include the 80% participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains, the 80% exemption for qualifying net intellectual property income, and statutory investment tax credits. Luxembourg CIT losses are normally carried forward indefinitely with a 70% offset cap on taxable income exceeding EUR 200,000; the 5-year figure in this schema is a normalisation field and does not restate the Luxembourg statutory carryforward period.
